newsitem.title: UK: Stinking cheese may offer clue to mosquito traps.
newsitem.headline: Stinking cheese may offer clue to mosquito traps.

text.p: Scientists from around the world are flocking to Africa with bundles of stinky cheese to test the hypothesis that mosquitoes like smelly feet, a Dutch entomologist said on Friday.

"I have been informed that medical entomologists are now buying Limburger cheese and taking it to mosquito-infested areas around the globe," Bart Knols of Wageningen Agricultural University wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.
They hope to isolate whatever chemical it is that strong cheese and unclean feet have in common and use it to bait mosquito traps, Knols said.
The ideas are based on research showing that it is smell that attracts the hungry female mosquitoes.

"We have shown that three different Anopheles mosquitoes (a species that carries malaria) prefer to bite different parts of a naked motionless volunteer and that this behaviour is influenced by odours from those body regions," Knols wrote.

Other scientists have noted that ripening Limburger cheese smells just like odoriferous human feet, and Knols said they were beginning to work on isolating the precise combination of fatty acids that sends mosquitoes to olfactory heaven.

"Its use as a mosquito attractant may only apply as a result of the evolution of the intricate relationship between the African malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae and the odour of human feet," suggesting that primitive humans may have had smelly feet, Knols wrote.
